newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech parliament nears final vote on 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Czech parliament nears final vote on 1997 budget.

text.p: The lower house of Czech Parliament is expected to take a final vote on the 1997 budget on Friday, and it is likely to win approval despite wrangling in the centre-right ruling coalition this week.
Debate on the third and final reading of the budget can start, according to rules of the parliament, after 1330 local time (1230 GMT), 48 hours after debate ended on the second reading on Wednesday.
A vote could come as early as Friday afternoon, or could be extended into next week.

After an agreement of the three coalition parties to support the budget on Thursday, the minority government needs two opposition votes to assure approval of the planned balanced budget of 549.1 billion crowns, up from 491 billion in 1996.

The coalition led by the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus fell two seats short of a majority in the 200-seat Chamber in June elections, and the budget vote is seen as crucial to the survival of the minority government.
But in October four members of the opposition Social Democrats broke party ranks to allow the draft 1997 budget to get through the parliament's first reading.
Observers widely expect the budget to be approved, as there are no signs that the opposition deputies have dropped their support, although the margin still would be very narrow.

On Thursday coalition leaders said they had reached a compromise after a junior partner, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), demanded a commitment to a deregulation plan on energy and housing rents and tax cuts.
The three party leaders agreed to appease ODA by completing the deregulations and tax cut schedule by the year 2000, the end of the government's current term.
If the government budget plan is approved, it would be the fifth straight balanced budget under the leadership of Klaus, an avowed monetarist economist.
The government said on Wednesday, however, that the 1996 budget, which was approved as a balanced budget, may end with a deficit totalling 1.2 billion crowns.

The cabinet froze selected spending in December and will require early repayment from the state-managed deposit insurance fund on some state credits in order to keep the 1996 deficit from growing to between 3.2-5.2 billion crowns.
